g.id: Driven by: fall the route needs, minus fall the ground gives
A lift is forced the moment a chamber would pass 12 m
Fall needed = route length x flattest gradient allowed
LEVER: shorten and flatten the route
Each street drains to its NEAREST point on the main pipe
Route priced two ways - uphill costly, or trench depth costly
Streets that dug deep last attempt are made 8x costly, then retry
MEASURED: no main pipe 6 stations, main pipe 4
Full western main pipe: still 4, but properties pumped 1941 down to 1228
Driven by: ground that falls slower than the pipe must
Depth builds up going downstream and never recovers on its own
LEVER: lay at the FLATTEST gradient allowed, so the pipe stays high
55 percent of pipes are already at that flattest gradient
LEVER: take surplus fall as a DROP at the chamber, not a steep pipe
LEVER: route around high ground rather than under it
MEASURED: median depth 1.77 m - most of the network is shallow
BUT the deep tail is the whole problem
12 percent of chambers are over 6 m, and they hold 43 percent of all the digging
Smallest size that keeps flow depth under 0.65 and speed under 3 m/s
Size is set by the flow, then checked against the limits
Judged on the TRUE bore, not the nominal name
Rule blocks the usual trick: pipes shall NOT be oversized to gain a flatter gradient
MEASURED: 94 percent of the network is already at DN200
DN200 is the guideline MINIMUM main size - it cannot go smaller
Pipes run about 5 percent full at the median - flow is not what sets the size
So pipe size is NOT a lever here. Only 3.5 km sits above DN200
Where the remaining gain actually is
Deep chambers come from route detour - still 1.35x straight line at best
One thing drives both the lifts AND the digging: the deep tail
And from deepening chambers so houses below road level can drain - that alone added a station
GAP: the search counts stations and properties pumped ONLY
It does not yet minimise trench volume, so a design that is shallower everywhere but keeps the same station count is not preferred
Adding trench volume to what is kept would attack the 43 percent directly
EFFICIENCY: fewer lifts, shallower trenches, smaller pipes
